verdict: Local dev server on localhost:3100 was unstable (503, a 404 on /, a goto timeout), so stabilise it and rerun; the delivery-date test separately points to a likely product bug.

failures.test: Delivery estimate › the delivery date range is calculated from the visitor's date after load
failures.summary: After load the delivery date never resolves, so the expected 'Oct 08-12' range is never rendered.
failures.evidence: Snapshot (HTTP 200, no page or console errors): term "Delivery Date:" → definition: Calculating delivery date. The same stuck text appears in the flaky test's snapshot, which did not fix the clock.
failures.next_step: Check the client-side delivery-date calculation on the product page and why it never replaces 'Calculating delivery date'. Also confirm it works with Playwright's page.clock.setFixedTime and with the '3-5 working days' rule the test assumes, given the page shows 'Within 4 Days'.

failures.test: Product info › quantity cannot go above the stock of the selected variant
failures.summary: The server returned 503, so the product page and #quantity input never rendered.
failures.evidence: lastNavigation status 503; snapshot: heading "Service Unavailable"; console: 'the server responded with a status of 503'
failures.next_step: Find out why the local server at localhost:3100 returns 503 (backend or dependency not ready, or crashing under load), then rerun.

failures.test: Smoke: site health › route responds: home (/)
failures.summary: The home route returned 404 on both attempts, while other tests loaded / with 200 in the same run.
failures.next_step: Check whether the smoke spec uses the same baseURL as the other tests and whether the server was fully up when it ran. If / really 404s on a healthy server, reclassify as product_bug.

failures.test: Product info › selecting a colour updates the stock for the selected size
failures.summary: The beforeEach page.goto timed out waiting for load, then the test passed on retry.
failures.evidence: TimeoutError: page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded … waiting until "load"; outcome flaky, passed on attempt 2
failures.next_step: Likely the same local server instability that caused the 503. Ensure the server is warmed up and healthy before the suite starts (e.g. a webServer health-check URL).
